newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares ended weaker on Thursday following another bad day on the bullion markets and a poor set of results from Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, dealers said.
The international price of the yellow metal hovered precariously near to the $340 an ounce level, spreading yet more doom and gloom in an index that has become well-used to bad news.
The bombed-out sector finished 2.1 points down at 1,250.6.
"There's no excuse for the golds to go up, the gold price is not offering any encouragement. If it breaks under 340 again they'll go with it," one dealer said.
There was also bad news from as Gold Fields posted its first quarter figures.
Dismal numbers knocked Kloof Gold Mining Company Ltd to a new year low on Thursday and analysts and dealers said this did not bode well for other gold mining shares.
Kloof halved its March quarter pre-capex profit to 54.63 million rand and the stock fell to 31.75 rand per share from its previous 32.90 rand close before climbing back to end at 32.00 rand.
"I would think this would be very worrying for other gold shares," said Nick Goodwin, analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.
Parent Gold Fields declared first quarter profit of 236.42 million rand -- a severe drop from its preceding quarter's 333.08 million rand.
But Gold Fields itself remained unmoved, not trading all day except for one trade of 200,000 shares shortly after its results which held the share steady at 108 rand.
Driefontein Consolidated fell 45 cents to end at 40.80 rand after it posted a fall in profit to 182.02 million rand from 214.09 million rand.
"It (the results) is not good for gold shares and we'll see them taking this to heart," one dealer said.

The rest of the market had a quiet day after a brief flurry of trade in the morning. Dealers had expected shares to gain strength from a more positive Wall Street, but no strong upward move ever materialised.

"Industrials were disappointing and should have moved with Wall Street but didn't. The mindset in the market is that the Dow is not yet out of its corrrective downward consolidation phase," said one dealer.
The industrials index ended up 10.4 points at 8,238.7 and the all-shares index drifted off 0.8 points to close at 6,976.
Amongst gainers were SA Breweries which put on 50 cents to 132.50 rand and Toco Holdings which added nine cents to 87 cents.
However, De Beers lost 250 cents to 162.50 rand while Barlows shed 125 cents to 47.75 rand.
Near-term equity index futures largely drifted, but the industrials contract edged up with some positive gains. However, volumes were thin.
The June gold futures were last at 870/885 from 872 settlement, industrial contracts stood at 8,085/95 from 8,063 and all-share contracts were at 6,495/510 from 6,465.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
